To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the multiplicity in Pb–Pb interactions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 5\, \mathrm{TeV}$ is expected to be lower than most of the predictions of the current models, and that this multiplicity can be measured with the ALICE detector using the multiplicity of the charged particles and the energy of the forward protons.

the multiplicity in Pb–Pb at the LHC will be lower than the predictions of most of the existing models, that the scaling of the charged particle multiplicity with the number of participating nucleons is not expected to be linear, and that a novel approach to multiplicity studies based on the effective energy is proposed.
the effective energy approach can be used to study particle production in very high energy pp collisions at the LHC and to predict the average charged multiplicities in Pb–Pb interactions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the properties of high-energy collisions at the LHC in the context of the limiting fragmentation hypothesis.
the development and implementation of a novel approach for the study of the multiplicity of particles produced in high energy heavy-ion collisions.
the study of particle production in hadron-hadron, nucleus-nucleus and nucleus-nucleus interactions at ultra-relativistic energies, using the ALICE apparatus at the CERN LHC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, if the universality picture is correct, then the expected multiplicity in AA collisions is significantly lower compared with most of the predictions of the models currently used.
the multiplicity of the charged particles in the central rapidity region of pp collisions at the LHC will be much higher than that expected for the most peripheral Pb–Pb interactions.

, in the framework of the limiting fragmentation hypothesis, the charged multiplicity in central AA collisions at LHC energies is expected to be significantly lower than the predictions from most of the models currently used in the literature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the multiplicity studies in pp collisions at the LHC can be very helpful in understanding the multiplicity evolution in ion–ion interactions at the same energy.
the effective energy approach is a very powerful method to estimate the multiplicity of the final state in AA interactions at the LHC.

the effective energy concept is a useful tool for the understanding of the particle production in the high-energy collisions, and it can also be used as a powerful tool for the study of the high-energy limit of QCD, which can be achieved at the LHC with the Pb–Pb interactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in spite of the large number of particles produced in AA collisions, the multiplicity is still a very important observable to be used to study the properties of the hot and dense medium formed in heavy ion collisions at the LHC.
the multiplicity in heavy-ion collisions at LHC is expected to be much smaller than the one predicted by models that assume a linear extrapolation of RHIC data to LHC energies.

the multiplicity of charged hadrons produced in Pb–Pb interactions at LHC is expected to be much lower than previously estimated, and that this will affect the interpretation of the results of ALICE and CMS in terms of the quark–gluon plasma properties.
